name: olai
//workspaces: TWO GLOBS, because the tenants nest. `packages/plugins/` is the plugin container and holds no package of its own — `olai-plugin-kolu` and `olai-plugin-odu` sit inside it — so `packages/*` alone would install a tree with both tenants missing, which is not a loud failure: bun would resolve `olai-plugin-kolu` off the registry, find nothing, and the first thing to say so would be a red install on somebody else's machine. THIS FIELD IS THE ONE SPELLING. The typecheck below takes a recursive glob that covers both without restating either; `scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh` reads this field with jq; and `packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts` derives its whole corpus from it. FOUR readers consume it and none of them writes a `packages/*` walk of its own: the typecheck above (one recursive filter), `scripts/workspace-members.sh` (the one shell expansion, which both `check-hydrated-deps.sh` and `prove-fence.sh` call), `packages/plugin-api/src/tree.testlib.ts` (the fence corpus — a `bun test` corpus that shelled out would make every equality depend on a subprocess) and `packages/acp/src/manifest.test.ts` (which cannot import the third, because its own first claim is that `@olai/acp` imports no `@olai` sibling). The last two are separate CODE and one RULE: refuse a glob shape you cannot expand, refuse one that matched nothing. That sentence read `Nothing else … writes a walk of its own` until a reviewer found acp still doing a one-level `readdirSync` — which was not a silent skip (its walk recurses, so tenant files were read) but a MISATTRIBUTION: both tenants keyed under a phantom `plugins`, and neither tenant a key at all. A glob copied is a glob that goes stale the next time the tree moves, and every one of those copies is GREEN when it does.

scripts.//typecheck: ONE glob, and a recursive one: `./packages/**` matches a top-level member and a nested tenant alike, so it does not have to be kept in step with the two globs above. `--filter .*.` would cover both too and is NOT used — it matches the ROOT package as well, whose `typecheck` script is this line, which re-enters itself. A member nobody typechecks is a member whose types are checked by whichever suite happens to import it.

//dependencies: The runtime dependencies of the hydrated @kolu/* sources, declared HERE at the root rather than in the member that imports them: the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) symlinks only the root package's direct dependencies into the root node_modules, and that is where node_modules/@kolu/<name>/src/*.ts resolves its own imports by walking up. Every entry is at the exact version the pinned kolu declares — PEER dependencies included, because a peer is a runtime import like any other and the arrangement it names (`the app supplies the runtime`) is exactly the one this list is. `ws` is here for that reason and not because any olai source imports it: @kolu/surface-app's serving half is a Node websocket server. `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` and `ts-pattern` are the same case one package over — @kolu/surface-mcp is built on the SDK's low-level Server and matches on its connection state with ts-pattern; no olai source imports either. This is not maintained by memory — scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh reads the pinned kolu's own answer out of the Nix store and fails `just check` when this list drifts from it. ONE script asks that of every pin: the same three assertions run again for `@odu/run-client` (the `odu-deps` leg), because a pin is a pin and the second one was a line-for-line copy of the first until it stopped being. `cosmokit` and `@standard-schema/spec` are the Cordis pin's turn of the same arrangement (`nix/cordis.nix`); drop both the day the spike is deleted.
//overrides: One effect instance, always. A transitive bump must not be able to smuggle in a second copy: Effect's error narrowing is `_tag`-structural precisely because two module instances would otherwise stop recognising each other's classes — and `instanceof`, Context keys and Schema identity do not even have that fallback. The @effect/platform-* packages carry tagged errors and Context tags of their own, so they are pinned beside it. Versions come from the pinned kolu, and THIS BLOCK is checked by scripts/check-hydrated-deps.sh alongside the dependency lists, for EVERY pin rather than only for kolu — it was not, for a while, which is the hole worth naming: an override is how bun silently rewrites a version, so an unchecked one makes every other manifest's honesty cosmetic; re-pinning kolu means re-running `just check` and moving whatever it names. @types/node is the same discipline for a different reason: bun-types and @types/ws declare `@types/node: *` and would otherwise nest 26.x, whose net.d.ts merges over 22's EventEmitter Server so a call to `.on` does not typecheck.
//devDependencies: @types/ws is the other half of the `ws` entry above: the hydrated sources are raw TypeScript, so `tsc --noEmit` checks them, and it resolves their types from the same root node_modules their imports resolve from.
